clue.text: Trail despoils, they say, after time

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the spelling of the word before may change
after tells us the sound-alike piece comes behind the time letter

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
rapes means despoils or plunders; respelt to match how it is pronounced

explanation.surface: A trail of destruction left by marauders, reported after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge wearily along, much as one might trail behind others on a long walk.

clue.text: Close encountered in an attempt to get in

indicators.note: something encountered within another thing sits inside it, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: an attempt is a try
a close is an end

explanation.surface: Someone meets a close shave while trying to break in somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' as a whole definition is easy to overlook: in the sense of 'in fashion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is in is currently fashionable, the same idea as trendy clothing or music.

clue.text: Rumbling tum is a childhood abnormality?

indicators.note: a rumbling stomach is churning, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried parent wonders whether a child's grumbling stomach signals something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the condition is a developmental difference usually identified in childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Autism is a developmental condition typically diagnosed in early years, which an older dictionary would describe as an abnormality.

clue.text: A keen Union man, they say Perkins failed utterly to accept Georgia

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so the name and the verb that follow are taken by their sound
to accept something is to take it in, so the state abbreviation goes inside

blocks.note: Pretty Polly Perkins of Paddington Green is the heroine of an old music-hall song
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state
failed means missed; utterly also says it is spoken

explanation.surface: A trade unionist recalls hearing that a woman called Perkins flopped in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Union is marriage, not a trade union: a man keen on it might take several wives.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygamist has multiple spouses at once, so he is cheekily described as very enthusiastic about wedlock.

clue.text: Set a clue in Western Australia

definitions.note: short for a place in Western Australia

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword setter composes a clue while living in Western Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Eucla is a tiny settlement on the Nullarbor Plain near the South Australian border.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucla is a remote township on the coast of that Australian state, so it lies within it.

clue.text: Confused by wild oat sown in 1 down?

indicators.note: wild suggests things running out of control, so these letters scatter into a fresh order
seed sown in soil ends up buried inside it, so these letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
1 down is TRENDY, and trendy means chic

explanation.surface: Puzzling over wild oats planted in some fashionable spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference means the answer to 1 down, which then has to be swapped for its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in total disorder, so a confused situation can be described with it.

clue.text: A sentence to be penned?

blocks.note: surface reading: a line of words to be written down with a pen
setter's reading: penned means locked up, so this is a court sentence served in prison

explanation.walkthrough: Penned looks like writing; it is confinement, as sheep are penned. A judge passes this kind of sentence when the offender goes to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodial sentence is one requiring imprisonment, so the offender is held in custody rather than fined.

clue.text: Growing culture revealed by Saga readers?

indicators.note: the answer is shown by the words that follow, lying in plain sight across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Fans of long family sagas uncovering a cultural trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is the jelly on which laboratory bacteria are cultivated, a medium for growing cultures.

clue.text: Secondary system's spasm circumscribes Scripture simpleton

indicators.note: to circumscribe is to draw a line around, so the spasm word surrounds the others

blocks.note: a tic is a muscular spasm
RI, religious instruction, was the old school name for Scripture lessons
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A twitch in a secondary school's timetable surrounds a dim pupil in RE.
explanation.walkthrough: Secondary is the old geological era (now the Mesozoic), and a system is the rock laid down in one period.
explanation.definitionFit: The Triassic is the first period of the Mesozoic, once called the Secondary era, and geologists call its rock strata a system.

clue.text: About ... about 100 kilos will be material

blocks.note: C is for circa, about
re means concerning
a metric ton, though that is really 1000 kilograms

explanation.surface: A rough guess that something weighs around a hundred kilos.
explanation.walkthrough: A tonne is 1000 kilograms, not 100, so the clue's figure is off by a factor of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy printed cotton fabric used for curtains and upholstery, so it is a material.

clue.text: Praise is, in this context, oleaginous

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters span the end of context and the start of oleaginous

explanation.surface: A remark that flattery, in this setting, is slimy and greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Oleaginous also means unctuous, which fits flattering praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, laud or glorify, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Choose the players to throw out

blocks.note: first meaning, read as three words
second meaning: discard

explanation.surface: A manager picks the team, only to drop some of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aside is to discard or reject; read as cast a side, it means selecting a team.

clue.text: He nominates doctor, one Greats don

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Oxford tutor in Greats is put forward for a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the Oxford classics degree and a don is a university teacher; doctor looks like a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A designator is someone who designates, that is names or appoints a person to a post.

clue.text: Run rings round Pole left here

definitions.note: a place: the clue as a whole points to where the Pole expedition left from

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the two circles enclose what follows

blocks.note: two rings are two circular letters
S for the South Pole
L for left

explanation.surface: Someone outpaces a Polish visitor who has just departed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a Polish person; with 'left here' the whole clue recalls Amundsen sailing from Norway's capital for the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Amundsen's expedition to the South Pole set off from Norway's capital, so it is the place where the Pole party left.

clue.text: Fellow-broker may be a gangster

blocks.note: a fellow is a male
a factor is an agent who buys and sells for others

explanation.surface: A warning that a fellow stockbroker could be a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer or criminal, and a gangster is one kind of criminal.

clue.text: Special scientific interest in genetic modification leads to muttering

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a mutation is a change to genes
the initials, as in SSSI, a Site of Special Scientific Interest

explanation.surface: Environmentalists grumble about GM crops near a protected site.
explanation.walkthrough: An SSSI is a protected conservation site in Britain; the clue drops its 'Site'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mussitation is a rare word for murmuring or moving the lips without clear speech, much like muttering.

clue.text: Where in the garden to bury herbs, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints the words are only one possible arrangement of these letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener asks where to plant herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area of a garden planted with bushes, so it is a place in the garden.

clue.text: One question about fruit is: "What is 21 on?"

indicators.note: about means around, so the fruit word wraps the first pieces

blocks.note: an apple is a fruit
Roman numeral one
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A quiz asking about a fruit and what it rests on.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is LAID: appliqué is decoration cut out and laid on, that is sewn on top of, another fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Appliqué is needlework where shapes of fabric are stitched on to a background, so it is work laid on.

clue.text: Choose to admit Henman is one to see the sunny side

definitions.text: one to see the sunny side

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the word for choose takes the others inside

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
Tim Henman, the British tennis player
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing to admit Henman is someone who always looks on the bright side.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was Britain's best-known tennis player around 2000, famously hopeful at Wimbledon.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimist expects things to turn out well, which is exactly looking on the bright or sunny side.

clue.text: Expectant boy and European girl set about stir-crazy night hunter

indicators.note: placed around something, so the boy and girl together enclose the rest
crazy means mixed-up, so this word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Pip is the hero of Great Expectations
taken as written
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman's boy and a girl go mad from being cooped up.
explanation.walkthrough: Expectant points to Dickens's Great Expectations; and stir is also slang for prison, making stir-crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipistrelle is a small bat that hunts insects at dusk and through the dark, so it is a nocturnal hunter.

clue.text: Set up an Italian city in the territory of Athens

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
città is Italian for city

explanation.surface: Founding an Italian city in ancient Greek lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Attica is the region of Greece around Athens, the city-state's home territory in classical times.

clue.text: Coming from no middle-aged outlet

indicators.note: having no middle means the central letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a vent is an opening for air or gas to escape

explanation.surface: Arriving from a shop that sells nothing to the middle-aged.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival, especially an awaited one, so it means a coming.

clue.text: Face up to being put down?

indicators.note: turned up means flipped over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a clock's face is its dial

explanation.surface: Confronting the experience of being belittled or humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: Face up to looks like confronting; it is a dial turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past participle of lay, so something laid has been placed or put down.

clue.text: Taken off in a reverie

blocks.note: first meaning: removed or extracted
second meaning: lost in thought, absent-minded

explanation.surface: Someone is carried away into a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to remove or extract something, and an abstracted person is preoccupied and dreamy.

clue.text: Maiden follows bear to the pole

definitions.note: the answer attaches to it, as in totem pole

indicators.note: follows puts the abbreviation behind the word for bear

blocks.note: to tote is to carry or bear
M for maiden, an over with no runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A young woman trails a bear on an Arctic trek.
explanation.walkthrough: Bear is a verb, not the animal; and pole is the carved post, not the North Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is the emblem carved on a totem pole, so it is what goes before that pole.

clue.text: Bones turn up when thus

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: as can mean when
so means thus

explanation.surface: Skeletons are unearthed in a certain way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for bone, used in medical terminology.

clue.text: Still leave off going around scene back to front

indicators.note: the back letter is brought round to the front of the word
going around means encircling, so the quitting word wraps the scene

blocks.note: to quit is to stop or leave off
its final E moved to the start

explanation.surface: An actor still has to walk off around the back of the stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiescent means inactive or at rest, so it matches still in the sense of motionless.

clue.text: Told to make an effort to exercise? Codswallop!

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the words are judged by how they are heard

blocks.clueFragment: to make an effort to exercise
blocks.note: try is make an effort; PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A gym teacher is told to put in effort, and dismisses it as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe and codswallop are both informal British words for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Mouth 1 down English?

blocks.note: first meaning: the wide mouth of a river meeting the sea
second meaning: 1 down is TRENDY, and ... English is the trendy accent of south-east England

explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is a London-and-Thames accent that became fashionable in the 1990s, even among the posh.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is where a river widens into the sea, and the word also names a fashionable British accent.

clue.text: Biting trill is heard

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the musical word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a mordent is a musical ornament, a quick trill-like alternation of notes

explanation.surface: A sharp, cutting trill of birdsong rings out.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is sharp and caustic, from the Latin for biting, so the adjectives are synonyms.
